fixtures.rationale: Casting through `any` silences the type checker instead of narrowing the value, so the function compiles without the caller ever proving `order` has a `grandTotal`.
The bare `@ts-ignore` silences whatever the checker was about to flag with no explanation of why that is safe.
Disabling the lint rule with no stated reason hides why the flagged code is actually fine.
The TODO stands in for the actual refund behaviour, so callers get the input echoed back with no indication anything is unfinished.
A bare not-implemented throw defers the real decision about what cancelling an order does to some future change.
The default branch does nothing and falls through to an implicit `undefined`, leaving the decision of what an unrecognized status should render unmade.
The suppression states exactly why it is safe and points to where the upstream gap is tracked, so the decision was made deliberately rather than deferred.
The default branch opens a block that asserts exhaustiveness with a `never` binding and throws, so nothing is silently skipped; the `default:\s*(break|return)?$` pattern does not match a block.

The value is cast to `unknown` right after crossing the JSON boundary and is narrowed by a runtime check before use; `as unknown` alone, without a further `as`, is not evidence of an omitted decision.
The non-null assertion asserts the cache always hits with no comment explaining why a miss can never happen here.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
